title: Temptation
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Temptation is the enticement to sin through disordered desire, deception, pressure, or opportunity. Temptation itself must be resisted through truth, watchfulness, prayer, and dependence on God’s grace.
summary: Temptation is the enticement to sin through disordered desire, deception, pressure, or opportunity. Temptation itself must be resisted through truth, watchfulness, prayer, and dependence on God’s grace.
christFocus: Jesus Christ was tempted yet without sin, and He helps His people in temptation. Through His victory, believers can resist sin and find mercy and grace in their time of need.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Temptation is not new. From Eden to the wilderness, Scripture shows temptation working through lies, desire, pressure, and misplaced trust. Temptation seeks to move the heart away from God’s Word and into sin.

God does not tempt anyone with evil. Temptation often arises as desire is drawn and enticed. If cherished and followed, desire gives birth to sin, and sin brings death.

Jesus faced real temptation and answered with Scripture. He trusted the Father where Adam failed and where Israel failed. His sinless endurance makes Him a merciful High Priest for tempted believers.

God provides help in temptation. Believers are called to watch and pray, resist the devil, flee sin, use Scripture, and trust that God is faithful to provide a way of escape.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Temptation often feels strongest when people are tired, wounded, hungry, lonely, angry, ashamed, or overconfident. This doctrine teaches believers not to be surprised by temptation or careless with desire.

It also protects from despair. Being tempted is not the same as surrendering to sin. Christ understands temptation, gives grace, and calls His people to resist rather than give up.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Take temptation seriously before it becomes sin. Watch your desires, pray early, use Scripture, flee what feeds sin, and seek help when needed. Do not trust your own strength; run to Christ, who was tempted without sin and gives mercy to those who come to Him.
